description: The main character is Kou Kitamura, son of the owner of Kitamura Sports. In the same neighborhood is a batting center run by the Tsukishima family. Due to their proximity and the relationship between their businesses, the Kitamura and Tsukishima families have been close for many years, with their children going back and forth between the two homes like extended family. Because Kou and Wakaba were the same age and always together, Aoba was jealous of all the time Kou spent with her older sister. Aoba is a natural pitcher with excellent form, and Kou secretly trains to become as good as she was, even while publicly showing little interest in baseball.

node.description: The third daughter of the Tsukishima family, one year younger than Kou and Wakaba. Aoba is jealous of how much time Wakaba spends with Kou, and frequently tells Kou how much she hates him. She is an excellent pitcher, Kou modeling after her. She has a poster of Ryota Igarashi, a famous fastball pitcher, hanging on her bedroom wall, and says she is only interested in a guy who can pitch a fastball at 160 km/h (about 100 mph). She loves to pitch in practice games, even though as a girl she cannot play in official baseball. However, she rarely shows her real speed, as most catchers can't handle it. Her name means "blue leaf". Upon entering high school, she has joined the baseball team, despite saying previously she would not.

In 5th grade in Part One, enters Seishuu High School at the start of Part Two. Kou lives down the street from the Tsukishima family and is treated like one of the family when he visits their house, batting cage, or coffee shop. He has been practically inseparable from [Wakaba](https://anilist.co/character/13285/Tsukishima-Wakaba) since their birth on the same day in the same hospital. While he shows little interest in baseball to outsiders, he has practiced daily at the Tsukishima Batting Center since he was old enough to swing a bat, enough so he is an excellent batter, especially against fastballs.

~! After Wakaba's death, Kou is inspired by [Aoba](https://anilist.co/character/13286/Tsukishima-Aoba)'s excellent pitching form to become a great pitcher himself, and secretly adopts Aoba's daily training regimen. Although he doesn't play baseball in junior high, his friends convince him to join the high school baseball club. Because Kou and his friends don't take the placement test, they are put on the second string team (called the "prefab" team). With his changeup fastball, he becomes a well-known ace pitcher in the eastern conference. !~

Position: First baseman   Younger brother of Junpei Azuma, in the same year as Kō. Yūhei was brought over to Seishū High School by Coach Daimon to play in his first-string team. He is an excellent batter, so he is the current cleanup hitter at Seishū. He has trouble recalling other people's names and faces, stating that he only remembers people that are worth caring for, but he apparently remembers Kō Kitamura. He has lost some of his confidence in Coach Daimon and the baseball team at the end of his first year, but seeing Kō's abilities during the practice game convinces him to stay in Seishū after Daimon is sacked.   Yūhei's obsession to reach Kōshien is due to his guilt towards Junpei Azuma, his older brother. Junpei injured his leg, ending his rising baseball career, while saving Yūhei from falling down a staircase. The guilt of ending his brother's career turns his desire to reach Kōshien into obsession. Also, since then, Yūhei has been very sensitive towards children who are playing around stairs and matters of when a person's recklessness effects more then themselves. Because of that, he is shown initially to be very cold and uncaring towards people around him, as he is only concerned with reaching Kōshien. He gradually begins to enjoy the game more, becoming less stern on outcome and more on performance, and make friends as Junpei's happiness becomes more sincere throughout the series; turning Kōshien more and more to a personal dream or goal rather then a amends to his brother. He has stated that he has romantic interests in Aoba.   (Source: Wikipedia)

Second daughter of the Tsukishima family, in 5th grade in Part One. Through their childhood, Wakaba is constantly with Kou. She constantly talks about their future together, even giving him a schedule of suggested future birthday gifts that includes an engagement ring for her 20th birthday. She frequently kisses Kou, which annoys their mutual friend Akaishi, who has a secret crush on her. For several birthdays in a row, Wakaba gives Kou alarm clocks because he has a hard time waking up in the morning.

Position: Catcher   Akaishi is a childhood friend of Kō and Wakaba, the same age as them. In Part One, he has a crush on Wakaba and is jealous of the time Kō spends with her. In elementary school, he was kept from pitching on his Little League team because he got into fights with opposing teams. He was able to throw a 100 km/h fastball while in elementary school, but Kō could hit a home run off one of his pitches. However, since Wakaba's death, he plays as a catcher to fulfill Wakaba's last dream in which he and Kō reach Kōshien with him being the catcher and Kō the pitcher. He is currently have feelings for Akane who look a lot like Wakaba. Because he did not take the placement test for the baseball club, he is on the prefab team with Kō. His father owns a liquor/sake store.   (Source: Wikipedia)

Fourth and youngest daughter of the Tsukishima family. She is in kindergarten during Part One, and in 5th grade at the start of Part Two. Although she lost her mother at a very young age, she has a happy, energetic, and outgoing personality. Despite their difference in ages, Momiji and Kō have a friendly, sibling-like relationship. She catches for him when he practices pitching. Once, while playing catch, Aoba apologizes for throwing the ball so hard and Momiji says she is used to it as Kō's pitches are harder—to Aoba's surprise. Momiji grows up to resemble her older sister Wakaba, which surprises Akaishi the first time he meets her. Her name means "maple leaf."

Akane bears an uncanny resemblance to [Wakaba Tsukishima](https://anilist.co/character/13285/Tsukishima-Wakaba). Her parents opened a soba restaurant next to Kitamura Sporting Goods shortly after Seishū's loss to Ryuō. She is an excellent artist, and won the grand prize of the Kōshien Poster Art Competition, using [Aoba](https://anilist.co/character/13286/Tsukishima-Aoba) as the model.

She is currently enrolled in Seisen Private Girl's Academy and is employed at Coffee Clover. She has suffered from an unknown disease since childhood and is often admitted into the hospital for various tests. She has stated that she is dating [Kō Kitamura](https://anilist.co/character/13230/Kitamura-Kou), but she seems to be very caring towards [Akaishi](https://anilist.co/character/21681/Akaishi-Osamu) as well.

Position: Batting Coach   Older brother to Yūhei Azuma, he was once a star pitcher and cleanup batter for Takao Jitsugyo High School. He was on the verge of winning the regional finals to reach Kōshien, as well as being observed by pro team scouts, but was forced to quit baseball after sustaining a career-stopping leg injury while saving Yūhei from falling down a staircase. He runs a produce delivery service, and is currently acting as the batting coach for Seishū's baseball team. This is because Ichiyō, whom he is romantically involved with, has promised to marry him if Seishū makes it to Kōshien.   (Source: Wikipedia)
The Tsukishima's black-and-white cat. He is named after Hideo Nomo, a former right-handed pitcher in Nippon Professional Baseball and Major League Baseball from Japan.

Position: Center Fielder, Pitcher   One of the ringers that Coach Daimon brings in. He is an excellent batter and plays in center field. However, he was demoted to bench-warmer after defying Daimon's orders to make the correct play. After the subsequent fallout with Coach Daimon, he transferred to Sena Municipal High School, becoming their ace pitcher and cleanup batter. He was also acting as a player-coach in his new school, since its baseball club did not have a proper coach. He eventually led his school to victory against his former coach's new school, Kurokoma Jitsugyō.   (Source: Wikipedia)

First daughter of the Tsukishima family. At the start of Part Two, she is in her third year of college. After her mother's death, she has run the Tsukishima household, acting as a surrogate mother for her sisters. She treats Kō like a younger brother. Her cooking is generally good, though she sometimes makes something wrong. She likes Junpei Azuma, but has trouble expressing her feelings to him directly. Her name means "first leaf".

Position: First baseman, Third baseman   A member of the Seishū High School baseball club, in the same year as Kō and Akaishi. He likes Kō, but has a rocky relationship with him ever since elementary school, when Kō convinced he and his friends to buy a lot of brand new baseball equipment from the Kitamura store. In compensation, Nakanishi forces Kō to learn the basics of baseball (outside of hitting). He joins the baseball club in junior high, but quits after three months, getting into a bloody fight with the slacking seniors. However, he keeps training after leaving the club. He joins the baseball club in high school, but like Kō and Akaishi he does not take the placement test and is placed on prefab team. While he plays catcher in elementary school, in high school he originally plays first baseman before switching to third baseman as Azuma joins as first baseman.

Position: Shortstop   A member of the Seishū baseball club, in the same year as Kō. He is the only first-year student to pass the baseball club placement test, and therefore on the first-string team. Because of this, he frequently brags about how good he must be. Coach Maeda comments that Senda is too much of a showoff to be a good pitcher, but that he would likely make a great shortstop. He constantly pursues Aoba, trying to get her to date him. After making too many errors as pitcher, he is demoted to the prefab team, where he plays shortstop. After the sacking of coach Daimon, he becomes the starting player in Seishū baseball team. His appearance and personality are similar to Ryūtaro Kine from H2.   (Source: Wikipedia)

The current head coach of the Seishū baseball team. Because he has coached Seishū for so long, he is well-known and has a lot of influence with other coaches in the region. He is known to be a very lenient and 'weak' coach. He tends to prioritize the enjoyment of the game over victories, hence he always prioritizes the third-years in competitions.
Senda's cousin. She is in the 1st year at Satomi Girl’s High and challenges Aoba Tsukishima. She only appears in the anime.

Owner of Tsukishima Batting Center and the Clover coffee shop, and father of Ichiyo, Wakaba, Aoba, and Momiji. Both his wife and second daughter have died, but he is very nice and a worldly man. During high school, he played catcher on a team that went to Kōshien.

Manager of the prefab team, one year ahead of Kō. Despite being called "chubby" by some of the players, she has a kind heart and is a very hard worker. Just like Risa Shido, she is also a former foreign exchange student. However, as opposed to the arrogant Risa Shido, she is humble and down-to-earth. She is the granddaughter of the Seishu board chairman, but she never takes advantage of that fact.   (Source: Wikipedia)

Position: Third baseman   A member of the prefab team of the Seishū baseball club, two years ahead of Kō. He is always late. He did not get along with Nakanishi in junior high, and frequently pushed him around. He is jealous of Kō's abilities and lets it affect how he plays. He retires after the first practice game against the first-string team.   (Source: Wikipedia)

Position: Manager   Manager of the first string team under Coach Daimon, one year ahead of Kō, and daughter of the stand-in principal. She is a former foreign exchange student who recently returned to Japan. As she considers herself to be above the baseball players, she does not do any work and treats the team (especially the prefab members) as her personal servants. Despite being the manager of the first-string team, she has very little interest in or knowledge of baseball. During the rematch practice game between the first-string and prefab teams, she is on a vacation in Europe. When the regular principal returns, she is fired from the team and she begins working at her mother's boutique. Even after her parents divorce, she still tries to use their influence to get ahead. After she successfully passes an audition for a role in a TV drama, she quits the baseball team altogether and sets up her own fans club in school. However, she is shown to have a little bit of guilty conscience for never doing anything useful for the team as a manager.  

(Source: Wikipedia)
Nakanishi's girlfriend. She often asks Aoba for personal baseball matches, so she can improve.
Kou's father, owner of Kitamura Sporting Goods. He is a fan of the Tokyo Yakult Swallows baseball team.
Kou's mother. Aoba loves her korokke, and frequently visits the Kitamuras to obtain them.

Father of Risa and Acting Principal of Seishū, he is the one responsible for bringing in Coach Daimon. Like his daughter, he is only concerned with the prestige that comes with Kōshien, having no interest in baseball itself. After Daimon's team loses to the prefabs, he is unceremoniously transferred by Chairman Ōkubo following revelations of fiscal mismanagement.

Position: Coach   A nationally renowned coach, having reached Kōshien several times and won it twice. He was brought in by Vice-Principal Shidō to build up Seishū's baseball team, replacing Coach Maeno in the process. He also brought in his own ringers to create a first string team, relegating the existing baseball club to second string or prefab status (or, as he often called it, 'cesspool'). When his team lost to the prefabs in their rematch, he was forced to resign along with Shidō. He is currently the head coach for Kurokoma Jitsugyō, employing the same talent-buying strategy he used in Seishū.   (Source: Wikipedia)

Position: Second baseman   A member of the prefab team of the Seishū baseball club, two years ahead of Kō. Like Makihara, Sekiguchi didn't get along with Nakanishi in junior high. He retires after the first practice game against the first-string team.   (Source: Wikipedia)

Voiced by: Kyōsuke Suzuki  Position: Center fielder   A member of the prefab team of the Seishū baseball club, two years ahead of Kō. Tsuneki also didn't get along with Nakanishi in junior high. He is now retired from baseball. He retires after the first practice game against the first-string team.   (Source: Wikipedia)

Chair of the Seishū High School board and Hiroko Ōkubo's grandfather. He is a regular customer at Akaishi's father's sake store. He has a very stubborn personality and always keeps his promises. As board chair, he is a little worn out from worrying about Vice Principal Shidō (the temporary principal), though he does not let that show in public. During the first practice game between the first-string and prefab teams, he sneaks in the game with Aoba. During the rematch, he goes back and forth between the two teams' benches, and after the prefab team wins he enforces the agreement that the losing team be dissolved.   (Source: Wikipedia)

The Tsukishima sisters' cousin from their mother's side. Mizuki's father, Isamu Asami, is a younger brother of Yōko Tsukishima. He is a world-renowned mountain climber and often travels around the world. As a result, Mizuki becomes an excellent climber too and has been raised overseas most of his life. However, he wants to at least finish his high school in Japan. Thus, he enrolls in Seishū and stays with the Tsukishimas. A kind and honest person, he is very popular with girls in Seishū, but he has stated that he is only interested in Aoba Tsukishima. He sees Yūhei Azuma as his rival on Aoba. He is in Seishū mountaineering club, although he is always having his own activities as the club activities is below his expectations. He is often seen climbing tall structures, such as poles and school buildings, without any equipment.    (Source: Wikipedia)
Ryuō's star batter.    ~!He fractures one of his fingers during the match against Seishu. He has to drop out of the game and give his spot up to to Mishima, much to his dismay. !~
Father of Youko Tsukishima and Isamu Asami.
Mother of Youko Tsukishima and Isamu Asami.
Shortstop Kishibe he was an ace fourth batter in middle school.
Ace, Kamikawa, Fastballs and curve balls are his specialties.
Ryuoh's left-hander pitcher.
Sannoh's coach. Proclaims that [Kou](https://anilist.co/character/13230) is "a pitcher that comes once every 10 years".
Ryuoh's right-hander pitcher.
Seishu's baseball player. He is in the same year as Aoba Tsukishima.
Seishuu Academy Middle School baseball team head coach.
Old man from Onnen, he appears in Volume 6 chapter 39 and in episode 13 and is voiced by Masako Nozawa.  Aoba and Kou thinks that he is an Old Lady.
Megumi Shimano is a baseball player of Ryuō Academy's female baseball team, she's a very good player as her cousin, Tadashi Shimano also a baseball player at Ryuō's main team.
